The National Youth Service Corps has taken free medical services to residents of the Abiriba community in the Ohafia Local Government Area of Abia State, as part of its third Quarter 2026 Health Initiative for Rural Dwellers. The outreach, held at Erinma Hall, Abiriba, was organised to bring accessible healthcare closer to rural residents, particularly those in underserved communities who face challenges accessing basic medical facilities. Speaking at the flag-off ceremony, on Thursday the Abia State NYSC Coordinator, Yunusa Tanimu, said the initiative was designed to complement the efforts of the federal and state governments towards achieving universal health coverage. “This initiative is designed to ensure that more Nigerians have access to quality healthcare irrespective of their location or economic circumstances,” Tanimu said. He explained that the HIRD programme, launched in 2014, provides free medical consultations, examinations, treatments and medications to rural communities across the country. The coordinator disclosed that the medical team comprised doctors, nurses, pharmacists, medical laboratory scientists and other healthcare professionals drawn from NYSC medical personnel. He added that the exercise was open to everyone, regardless of their medical complaints, and assured residents that cases beyond the capacity of the outreach team would be referred to appropriate health facilities. I encourage residents, particularly elderly persons, women, children and other vulnerable members of the community, to take advantage of this opportunity,” Tanimu said. He also appealed to philanthropists, corporate organisations and well-meaning Nigerians to partner with the NYSC to sustain the initiative. “Additional support will enable us to reach more underserved communities,” he added. Also speaking, the Zonal Inspector of NYSC in Ohafia Zone, Michael Chukwueze, described the exercise as a timely health intervention for rural dwellers. “Beneficiaries received free medical treatment and medications from NYSC medical personnel. I urge residents to appreciate the NYSC and make good use of this opportunity,” Chukwueze said. One of the beneficiaries, 53-year-old Enyinnaya Ogele, expressed appreciation for the intervention, revealing that he received medical attention for an eye problem. “I came with an eye problem. I was attended to, given medication and referred to a higher medical facility for further examination and treatment. I am grateful for the NYSC,” Ogele said. The Third Quarter 2026 HIRD outreach in Abiriba forms part of the NYSC’s broader commitment to community development, grassroots healthcare delivery and improving access to essential medical services among rural populations.
